comment: Pages whose WORDING this site depends on, watched for change.
The link checker only proves a URL still resolves. That is not enough: the
damage this project has already done to itself came from a page that stayed
at the same address and changed what it said. A reader can be sent to an
exam that is not accepted, or kept away from one that is, by a single
Each entry lists words that must still be PRESENT and words that must still
be ABSENT. When one flips, the workflow opens an issue naming the page.
A failed fetch is only ever a warning: a checker that cries wolf is one
An entry with "expect": "unreachable" is watched the other way round. It is
a site that is down now, and the event is it coming back — because what this
site says about that organisation came from somewhere else, and the day they
publish again their own words outrank ours.

pages.why: The list of accepted language-certificate providers on this page is load-bearing for the exam and visa pages. It changed between 24 September and 9 October 2026, growing from three names to five: VHS Kathmandu, IISC Study Hub and ECL were added. Watched so the next change is noticed in a day rather than a fortnight.

NSST told us on 9 October 2026 that their own site is being rebuilt and is not online, so everything the programmes page says about them rests on their letter. The day they publish again, every claim has to be re-checked against it — including the 18-25 age band, which is still 2023 material.
The second address NSST have used. It returned a 504 gateway timeout on 23 August 2026. Watched alongside thensst.org because either could come back first.

The au-pair page names only VHS Bhaktapur and the Goethe-Zentrum for the A1 certificate, while the national-visa page now names five providers. The au-pair page governs au-pair applications, so the site tells readers not to borrow the longer list. Watched for the day the two pages are brought into line.
present: A1 Level at VHS Bhaktapur or Goethe Centre Kathmandu
